title: Find a boundary that can own a business fact
description: Switch scenarios to compare a modular monolith, a useful fulfillment extraction, and the shared-database anti-pattern. Select a component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Shopper
nodes.detail: Starts checkout and needs one clear answer about whether the order was accepted and when it can arrive.

nodes.label: Checkout module
nodes.detail: Validates the cart, creates the order record, and owns the customer-facing order state. It must not update inventory tables directly after extraction.

nodes.label: Order store
nodes.detail: Stores accepted orders, their reservation reference, and the outbox record that makes later event delivery durable.

nodes.label: Fulfillment service
nodes.detail: Owns availability and reservation decisions. Its public contract accepts an idempotent reservation command and returns a reservation result.

nodes.label: Inventory store
nodes.detail: Contains stock and reservation state. Only fulfillment writes here; other services learn facts through contracts or published events.

nodes.label: Order outbox
nodes.detail: Commits an order event with the order write so a transient broker outage cannot erase the fact that another service needs to learn.

nodes.label: Domain events
nodes.detail: Carries published order facts to consumers that can tolerate asynchronous delivery and independently replay or reconcile their local view.

scenarios.label: Modular monolith
scenarios.summary: Checkout and fulfillment are separate modules in one deployable. Their module APIs make ownership visible while a local transaction still protects the current invariant.
scenarios.result: This is a valid starting point: the boundary is tested without paying for network failure, distributed tracing, or data synchronization yet.

scenarios.label: Useful extraction
scenarios.summary: Fulfillment becomes independently deployable and owns its inventory store. Checkout calls its reservation contract and records the resulting reference with the order.
scenarios.result: There is now one write owner for stock. The asynchronous order event supports other consumers without making them part of checkout's response path.

scenarios.label: Shared database
scenarios.summary: Checkout calls a service but continues to write inventory rows directly. The apparent service boundary has not transferred authority or reduced coordination.
scenarios.result: This split adds a network dependency while preserving hidden coupling. Schema changes and correctness incidents still require joint coordination.
